cards.claim: You cannot hibernate an instance that is in an Auto Scaling group: if you try, Auto Scaling marks the stopped instance unhealthy and might terminate it and launch a replacement.
cards.scope: per instance in an Auto Scaling group.

cards.claim: An account created on or after June 1, 2023 cannot create a launch configuration in the console.
cards.scope: per account, by account creation date.

cards.claim: Accounts created on or after October 1, 2024 cannot create new launch configurations by any method (console, API, AWS CLI, or CloudFormation); the earlier block, for accounts created on or after June 1, 2023, covered the console only.
cards.scope: per account, by account creation date.
links: [cannot create new launch configurations using any method](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-launch-configurations-blocked-for-new-accounts)
[cannot create new launch configurations using the console](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-launch-configurations-blocked-for-new-accounts)
cards.changed: 2024-10-01: was cannot create new launch configurations using the console

cards.claim: For a group to scale in to 0 when no requests arrive, its minimum capacity must be set to 0.
Backlog per instance is the queue length (ApproximateNumberOfMessages) divided by the number of InService instances; the target tracking target is the acceptable backlog per instance.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group that processes an Amazon SQS queue.
links: [Divide that number by the fleet's running capacity](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-sqs-backlog-per-instance)

cards.claim: An instance refresh can help you deploy a new AMI or user data script across the group, migrate instances to new instance types, or switch a group from a launch configuration to a launch template.
A predictive scaling policy needs at least 24 hours of metric data before it can start forecasting.
cards.scope: per predictive scaling policy; minimum; not adjustable.
spoken: at least twenty-four hours of data

cards.claim: A new Auto Scaling group that replaces an old one needs 24 hours of historical load data before predictive scaling can generate forecasts again.
spoken: twenty-four hours of historical load data

cards.claim: By default an Auto Scaling group has no instance maintenance policy, so it handles instance maintenance events with the default behaviors.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: Since November 15, 2023 an instance maintenance policy lets you choose whether replacement instances launch before or after existing instances are terminated, for events such as an instance refresh or a health check replacement.
links: [launched before or after existing instances are terminated](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-change-instance-maintenance-policy-2023)

cards.claim: By default, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling replaces up to 10 percent of the group's desired capacity at a time until all unhealthy instances are replaced; in a group so small that 10 percent is less than one instance it replaces them one at a time, and an instance maintenance policy can modify the 10 percent value.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group; default; adjustable; groups where 10 percent of desired capacity is at least one instance; no instance maintenance policy changes the rate.

cards.claim: When an InService instance is unhealthy, EC2 Auto Scaling replaces it to keep the desired capacity, and the new instance launches with the group's current settings and its current launch template or launch configuration.
When the group receives traffic from an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer, EC2 Auto Scaling registers a new instance with the load balancer before marking it InService.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group with a load balancer.

cards.claim: Amazon EC2 status checks and scheduled events are the default health check type of an Auto Scaling group.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: EC2 Auto Scaling does not perform health checks on an instance in Standby; its health status stays what it was before standby until you return it to service.
A Standby instance remains part of the group but does not handle load balancer traffic, and the group will not terminate it through health checks or scale-in events.
To take an instance out of a group temporarily, AWS recommends the standby procedure rather than detaching and re-attaching it to the same group.
An instance in Standby is still managed by the Auto Scaling group but is not an active part of the application until you return it to service.
You are billed for instances that are in a standby state.
By default a lifecycle hook added in the console sends its notifications to EventBridge; to send them directly to SNS, SQS or Lambda you add the hook with the CLI, CloudFormation or an SDK.
cards.scope: per lifecycle hook created in the console; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: A lifecycle hook notification can target Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, or AWS Lambda directly.

A user data script can perform custom actions on instances as they launch without a notification target; to signal that the lifecycle action is complete, the script must call CompleteLifecycleAction, and you must create an IAM role with a policy that allows the instances to call this API.
links: [do not need to configure a notification target](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-lifecycle-hook-user-data-complete)

cards.claim: For large-scale replacement such as losing a whole Availability Zone, Well-Architected prefers static stability for high availability.
Scale-in protection does not stop manual termination through the EC2 console, CLI or API; to protect group instances from manual termination, enable EC2 termination protection.
links: [To protect Auto Scaling instances from manual termination](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-scale-in-protection-ec2-termination-protection-for-manual)

cards.claim: Termination protection is disabled by default; when enabled, it does not prevent AWS from terminating the instance for a scheduled event or Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling from terminating it when unhealthy or during scale-in.
cards.scope: termination protection on an EC2 instance; default; adjustable.
links: [does not prevent AWS from terminating the instance](../facts/ec2.md#ec2-termination-protection-default-off-not-asg)
spoken: termination protection is off by default
it does not stop Auto Scaling

cards.claim: The Amazon EBS health check type checks whether EBS volumes are reachable and pass I/O status checks; you must turn it on for the group.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: The VPC Lattice health check type checks whether VPC Lattice reports the instance as healthy; like the ELB check, you must turn it on for the group.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: Reserved Instance discounts apply to On-Demand Instances that a group launches: if you hold RIs for an instance family and EC2 Auto Scaling launches a matching instance, you receive RI pricing.
cards.scope: per account; the launched instance matches the Reserved Instance.

cards.claim: The default instance warmup is how long an instance waits after reaching InService before its usage data counts in the aggregated metrics, so new instances with temporarily high startup usage do not distort dynamic scaling.
Without an instance maintenance policy, the maximum healthy percentage of an instance refresh defaults to 100 percent.
cards.scope: per instance refresh; default; adjustable; no instance maintenance policy is set.

cards.claim: The Launch before terminating option provisions a new instance before an existing one can be terminated; it favors availability over cost savings.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group with an instance maintenance policy.

cards.claim: The Terminate and launch option of an instance maintenance policy provisions new instances at the same time existing ones are terminated; it favors cost savings over availability.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group with an instance maintenance policy.

cards.claim: An instance maintenance policy (added November 15, 2023) sets a minimum and maximum healthy percentage; the group replaces instances only within that range, so it can launch a new instance and wait for it to be ready before terminating the unhealthy one.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group with an instance maintenance policy.

cards.claim: On scale out, EC2 Auto Scaling does not count a new instance toward the group's aggregated metrics until it is InService and its instance warmup has finished.
Step scaling increases and decreases the group's current capacity using a set of step adjustments that vary with the size of the alarm breach.

With a load balancer attached, instances that the group launches are registered with the load balancer automatically, and instances it terminates are deregistered automatically; you do not register instances one by one.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group with a load balancer.

cards.claim: Once ELB health checks are turned on for the group, an instance that Elastic Load Balancing reports as Unhealthy is marked Unhealthy at the next periodic health check and replaced.

An unhealthy instance is one whose hardware has become impaired, or one that is not passing a user-configured ELB health check; EC2 Auto Scaling checks each instance at regular intervals and can also run ELB health checks when the instance is connected to a load balancer.
An instance affected by an EC2 scheduled event is considered unhealthy and replaced; it does not start shutting down until the time in the event timestamp.
cards.scope: per instance affected by an EC2 scheduled event.

cards.claim: If EC2 Auto Scaling detects that an instance is no longer in the running state, it treats this as an immediate failure, marks the instance Unhealthy at once and replaces it.
With an EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING lifecycle hook, an instance moves from Terminating to Terminating:Wait, then to Terminating:Proceed after you complete the lifecycle action, and then to Terminated.
cards.scope: per instance with a termination lifecycle hook.

cards.claim: With an EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING lifecycle hook, a new instance moves from Pending to Pending:Wait, then to Pending:Proceed after you complete the lifecycle action, and then to InService.
cards.scope: per instance with a launch lifecycle hook.

cards.claim: After a group launches or terminates instances, further scaling activities started by simple scaling policies wait for the cooldown period to end.
spoken: scaling activities started by simple scaling policies

cards.claim: Scheduled scaling and scaling policies can be used together on one group: after a scheduled action runs, the scaling policy keeps deciding whether to scale further, while capacity must stay within the minimum and maximum set by the scheduled action.
links: [must fall within the minimum and maximum capacity](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-plus-policies-together)

cards.claim: A scheduled action that does not set new minimum and maximum sizes keeps the group's current minimum and maximum limits.
A warm pool is a pool of pre-initialized EC2 instances beside an Auto Scaling group; on scale out the group draws on the pool, and instances count toward desired capacity only as they leave the pool.
To roll out code changes to multiple instances in a group, use AWS CodeDeploy or CloudFormation.
Without an instance maintenance policy, the minimum healthy percentage of an instance refresh defaults to 90 percent.
cards.scope: per instance refresh; default; adjustable; no instance maintenance policy is set.

cards.claim: With a minimum healthy percentage of 90 percent and a maximum healthy percentage of 100 percent, an instance refresh replaces 10 percent of capacity at a time.
When you change a group's launch configuration, new instances launch with the new configuration, but existing instances are not affected.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group that uses a launch configuration.

cards.claim: By default, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling ignores the results of Elastic Load Balancing health checks.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group; default; adjustable.
links: [ignores the results of the Elastic Load Balancing](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-elb-health-checks-ignored-by-default)
spoken: ignores the load balancer health checks

cards.claim: An Auto Scaling group keeps a fixed number of instances even when one becomes unhealthy: it terminates the unhealthy instance and launches another to replace it.
Until its warmup time has expired, a new instance is not counted toward the group's aggregated EC2 instance metrics.
links: [not counted toward the aggregated EC2 instance metrics](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-warmup-instance-not-in-metrics)
spoken: not counted in the aggregated metrics

cards.claim: A custom health check can mark an instance Unhealthy (for example with set-instance-health), which makes EC2 Auto Scaling replace it immediately.

A single Auto Scaling group can provision and scale EC2 capacity across different instance types, Availability Zones, and On-Demand, RI and Spot purchase options, with a chosen split between On-Demand and Spot capacity.
Each step scaling policy holds up to 20 step adjustments, and this quota is not adjustable.
cards.scope: per step scaling policy; maximum; not adjustable.

cards.claim: The Elastic Load Balancing health check type checks whether the load balancer reports the instance as healthy and able to handle requests; you must turn it on for the group.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: A lifecycle action ends with continue or abandon: at launch, continue puts the instance in service and abandon lets the group terminate and replace it; at termination both let the instance terminate, and abandon skips remaining hooks.
links: [abandon indicates that your custom actions were unsuccessful](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-lifecycle-hook-abandon-continue)

cards.claim: When a lifecycle hook's timeout elapses or an unexpected failure occurs, the Auto Scaling group takes the hook's default result, and that default value is ABANDON.
